newsitem.title: UK: T-bonds dip in London, see modest auction result.
newsitem.headline: T-bonds dip in London, see modest auction result.

text.p: U.S. Treasuries in London ticked lower on Tuesday, ahead of the quarterly refunding due to kick off later with a three-year note auction.
Traders said the $16 billion note sale should be well absorbed but with three-year yields hovering just below 6.0 percent, the extent of oversubscription could be limited.
"It may not be too bad. But it's probably one of the more difficult of the three because the yields are so thin at the moment," said Andrew Davies, bond analyst at London Bond Broking.

By 1000 GMT, the 30-year long bond was quoted at 101-27 yielding 6.48 percent, from 101-28 in Tokyo and 101-29 in New York at the close. The three-year note was at 100-30, yielding 5.99 percent against 100-31 in New York.
The Treasury refunding will continue on Wednesday with a $12 billion offer of 10-year notes, followed by an issue of $10 billion in 30-year bonds on Thursday.
"We have been trading in a three-tick range," said one London dealer, adding trading conditions were quiet after two-day heavy losses.
But the market, bruised after Friday's sell-off on stronger than expected U.S. data, would likely remain under pressure from this week's supply, although cheaper prices should also tempt buyers.
"The market is now at a significantly lower level than when the refunding was announced. In those circumstances the overall shape of the refunding should be quite reasonable," said Davies.

No major data are due to be released this week, but on Wednesday the Federal Reserve's Beige Book of economic conditions is expected to set the scene for the Federal Open Market Committee (FOMC) meeting on August 19.

Economists expected the Fed to hold rates steady at that meeting, but added any new evidence in the Beige Book that tightness in the labour market is feeding through to higher wages could upset the market.
On Tuesday, the June leading indicator is due at 1400 GMT, BTM/Shroders weekly survey is at 1300 GMT while the Redbook Retail Sales Index is at 1855 GMT.
In the futures market, September T-bonds were down 2/32 on the day at 114-19 in automated trade.
